name: Creator / content-business bundle
description: A third base bundle targeting solo creators, indie publishers, and content-led small businesses. Distinct from the business bundle's developer/solopreneur focus: audience is writers, marketers, and newsletter/YouTube/substack operators who run a business on content + funnels, not on code. Candidate scenarios cluster neatly: seo-optimizer, landing-manager, landing-page-business-suite, campaign-content-studio, brand-manager, funnel-builder, social-media-scheduler, notes, chart-generator, palette-gen.
acquisitionHypothesis: Creators already pay a stack of $20-$50/mo tools (Ghost, ConvertKit, Buffer, Descript, Beehiiv, Canva). An integrated bundle where agents move context across draft -> landing page -> campaign -> analytics compresses that stack AND adds agent assistance the individual tools don't have. Hero acquisition scenario is likely campaign-content-studio or landing-page-business-suite.
retentionHypothesis: Creators live in a weekly produce-publish-distribute-measure loop. Once agents learn brand voice, posting cadence, and audience patterns, migration cost out compounds weekly. Every published asset becomes durable context the agents reuse - the opposite of Buffer, which has zero memory across weeks.
revisitTrigger: Revisit when business bundle has >=25 paying subs AND >=4 of the creator-cluster scenarios (seo-optimizer, landing-manager, campaign-content-studio, brand-manager, funnel-builder, social-media-scheduler) are `shipped` in their own PRDs.
signal: self-generated (capability-arrival derived from scenarios/ inventory; 7+ creator-stack scenarios exist or are planned)

name: AI quality and red-team add-on (business)
description: Add-on for business-bundle subscribers shipping AI features of their own. Bundles prompt-injection-arena, llm-evaluator, scenario-auditor, scenario-completeness-scoring, development-toolchain-validator into a coherent 'eval and harden your AI app' workflow. As EU AI Act and state-level AI liability rules tighten, indie devs and small shops need eval + red-team capability but can't afford a specialist; an integrated, local-first add-on fills that gap.
acquisitionHypothesis: Developers shipping AI-powered features increasingly face 'prove it's safe' pressure from customers, app stores, enterprise buyers, and (increasingly) regulators. A turnkey eval + red-team surface with regression diffs is legible value in a market that currently requires stitching together Braintrust / Patronus / Promptfoo / homegrown scripts.
retentionHypothesis: Eval suites grow with the product - once a subscriber has logged 200 red-team cases and a regression baseline, leaving means rebuilding that corpus elsewhere. This is the same structural retention that APM tools (Datadog, Sentry) enjoy.
revisitTrigger: Revisit when business bundle has >=15 paying subs AND (prompt-injection-arena and llm-evaluator are both `shipped` OR >=2 prospects explicitly ask for AI-eval tooling).
signal: self-generated (capability-arrival: 5 AI-quality scenarios exist; regulatory tailwind is external but uncited-for-this-entry)

name: Multi-platform publisher add-on (business)
description: Add-on for business-bundle subscribers who want to ship the apps they build across platforms without learning each packaging toolchain. Bundles scenario-to-desktop, scenario-to-android, scenario-to-ios, scenario-to-extension, scenario-to-mcp, scenario-to-cloud, deployment-manager, app-monitor into a coherent 'author once, ship everywhere, observe it after' flow. Especially compelling when agent-manager + git-control-tower mature - the headliner subscriber is already building apps and the publisher add-on is the natural expansion.
acquisitionHypothesis: The indie-developer pain of 'I built the thing, now getting it onto the Mac App Store / Play Store / Chrome Web Store / internally is another 3 weeks of yak-shaving' is universal. An integrated publisher layer is a tangible time-save with a clear before/after story.
retentionHypothesis: Every shipped app becomes a configured pipeline - signing keys, store metadata, telemetry wiring, update manifests. Churning means reconfiguring every pipeline elsewhere. High switching cost grows with app count.
revisitTrigger: Revisit when business bundle has >=25 paying subs AND >=3 of (scenario-to-desktop, scenario-to-android, scenario-to-ios, scenario-to-extension, scenario-to-mcp) are `shipped`.
signal: self-generated (capability-arrival: 6 scenario-to-X scenarios exist; agent-manager path will make this high-leverage)

name: Smart-home / household-operations add-on (lifestyle)
description: Add-on for lifestyle-bundle subscribers that coordinates a household's ambient systems: home-automation, device-sync-hub, lifestyle-dashboard, calendar, notification-hub, notes, maintenance-orchestrator. Not 'replace Home Assistant' - rather, 'give Home Assistant + your calendar + your family's notes a shared agent layer so routines, reminders, and household decisions use the full context.' Sits cleanly adjacent to (not overlapping with) elder-care and family-with-kids add-ons.
acquisitionHypothesis: Smart-home enthusiasts are underserved by cloud SaaS for privacy reasons and underserved by Home Assistant's power-user posture. A local-first add-on that is conversational and context-aware (agents know the family's calendar, the maintenance schedule, and the household's notes) is a different-shaped product than the options they have today.
retentionHypothesis: Once household routines, device topology, and maintenance cadence are encoded, the add-on accumulates state that is deeply personal and hard to re-create. Churn means re-teaching a new system what the household is. This is the strongest kind of retention - personal context.
revisitTrigger: Revisit when lifestyle bundle is `active` AND (home-automation and device-sync-hub are both `shipped` OR a Tier 4 hardware appliance path activates - whichever first).
signal: self-generated (capability-arrival: 7 household-ops scenarios exist; complements but does not duplicate elder-care/family-with-kids)

Our pitch: same deliverable, backed by agents that keep working after handoff, with a clear path to a monthly subscription to continue iterating. The upfront-cash economics are competitive with agencies while the ongoing-tool economics beat them.

description: A third base bundle for households running ambient operations: family calendaring, shared notes, photo/file management, household devices, password/secrets, media, network monitoring, recipe and meal planning, household maintenance routines. Distinct from lifestyle bundle's individual focus: this is the multi-person household substrate that elder-care and family-with-kids add-ons can sit on (replacing or co-existing with the planned lifestyle bundle). Operator already filed family-bundle-media-server as a backlog idea at vision walk #4 (2026-04-27) and articulated the homelab-app-scenario-seeding research method, signaling family-bundle is on the operator's planning radar as a candidate base bundle.
acquisitionHypothesis: The self-hosted/homelab audience is large, growing (the source X post about Claude-Code-built homelabs went viral), and structurally underserved by cloud SaaS - both for privacy reasons and because each tool is run in isolation today. An integrated family-substrate bundle where the household's calendar + notes + photos + devices share an agent layer is a category that doesn't exist yet on the consumer side. Hero acquisition scenario likely home-automation or bookmark-intelligence-hub.
retentionHypothesis: Households accumulate years of state - photos, notes, routines, device topology, recipes, kids' info. Once the agent layer learns the household's patterns, switching cost is enormous and personal. This is even higher-retention than smart-home-add-on alone because it spans more of the household's daily life.

name: Home-inspection vertical (dual-audience)
description: Vertical-compliance overlay built on the future regulatory-intel + BAS substrate, targeting home inspectors. Dual-audience product shape: paid pro tier (sold under business bundle or as standalone vertical SKU) for licensed home inspectors who need report templates, jurisdictional checklists, photo capture, client deliverables; free OSS tier for DIY homeowners who want to inspect their own property pre-purchase. The free tier is a credibility play and word-of-mouth lead-gen surface (user-of-the-tool friend recommends it to their inspector friend). OSS data-sovereignty positioning ('you own the data, not us, not your insurer') is unfakeable moat against Spectora/HomeGauge/ISN, who - per operator-captured TikTok signal - now resell inspection data to insurers.
acquisitionHypothesis: Pro-side: existing inspector software is consolidating, raising prices, and reselling data - actively pushing inspectors to look for alternatives right now (TikTok signal validates demand). Vrooli's OSS data-sovereignty pitch is structural and unfakeable, not a feature competitors can copy. DIY-side: home-buying is a high-stakes life event; a free, locally-run inspection assistant is shareable and aspirational. DIY is acquisition; pro is monetization.
retentionHypothesis: Pro: inspectors accumulate years of inspection records, photo libraries, jurisdictional templates, client list. Same compounding-state retention as other professional verticals. DIY: lower retention (one-off use per home purchase) but each DIY user is a referral seed.
